content.comment_body: I'm working on a very basic application where I want to send a voltage (such as 4V) to the analog output of a module, keep it active for 20 seconds, then turn it off. I was able to easily set the 4V using a PI controller block and entering the desired value into the manual output. However, when I tried using an off-delay timer for the 20-second interval, it didn’t function as expected. Is there a way to use a timer with this analog output module in [product_name]?
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. You actually don’t need a timer or PI controller in this situation. The solution is straightforward once you know how to approach it.

Thanks, [user_name]. Since I wasn’t familiar with the method, the solution wasn’t obvious and I ended up spending several hours finding a workaround, which was a good learning experience. In your circuit, what function does the AND (Edge) serve? It seems to work with or without it.

You're correct. But, without the AND (Edge) block, the off-delay timer only starts when the push button on input I1 is released. If someone holds the button longer, the output voltage remains active for more than 20 seconds, for example, 25 seconds.

Indeed, thanks again. I think similar logic is sometimes called a "one shot" in other product environments. (Although choosing products outside of [company_name]'s range is rare.) I'll start using AND (Edge) blocks in other push button circuits now. I appreciate the help—it’s been very useful as I was quite confused by this behavior.
